dedupe_keys.name: predstorm solar wind and geomagnetic storm prediction code

description: PREDSTORM is Python code for space weather prediction research that forecasts the background solar wind, high-speed streams and magnetic flux ropes of solar storms from monitors at the Sun-Earth L1 and L5 points and from any spacecraft east of the Sun-Earth line within about 1 AU. The Helioforecast group led by Christian Moestl develops it, with the copyright held by IWF-helio since 2019. From the predicted solar wind it derives the geomagnetic Dst index, Kp and auroral power, and a version for L5 and recurrence data runs in real time on the helioforecast.space site. Coverage is the near-Earth environment. Format and access: a public repository with conda environment files, relying on the Helio4Cast package for NOAA real-time files. Licence: MIT; free, and the authors ask to be contacted before results are used in peer-reviewed work. Caveats: it is research code, last updated in 2023, and forecast skill depends on upstream monitors. Dst and Kp forecasts feed geomagnetically induced current and satellite drag assessments for power grids and space assets. Related catalogue records are the OMNI solar wind data and the WSA-Enlil operational model.
